summary.headline: Deepak Nitrite Q1 FY27: record consolidated EBITDA of INR 554 crore (21% margin) and PAT of INR 345 crore, up 207% YoY.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue rose 35% YoY and 22% QoQ to INR 2,592 crore, with EBITDA up 159% YoY to INR 554 crore and margin at 21% versus 11% a year ago. Phenolics delivered record EBIT of INR 418 crore at a 24% margin, while Advanced Intermediates EBIT was INR 67 crore at an 8% margin. Management said April was disrupted by a maintenance shutdown, propylene shortages and gas curtailment, so the phenol run rate of about 1 lakh tonnes applies to parts of the quarter rather than the full period. Debt funding for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project has been closed, and the debt-to-equity ratio is 0.27x.

segments.name: Phenolics
segments.commentary: Record revenue of INR 1,775 crore and EBIT of INR 418 crore (24% margin), supported by stronger realisations, sustained demand and high utilisation. Management said the business is almost entirely domestic.

segments.name: Advanced Intermediates (AI)
segments.commentary: Revenue of INR 804 crore and EBIT of INR 67 crore (8% margin), helped by better realisations, higher operating rates and product mix. AI export mix is about 40-50%; raw material costs stayed high for some products.

guidance_outlook: MIBK and MIBC to be commissioned with acetophenone in August 2026; the remaining projects (multipurpose agrochemical intermediates facility, etc.) are due in Q2 FY27, with commercial volumes from January.
Management aims to reach 4 lakh tonnes of phenol in the existing Deepak Phenolics asset in the short to medium term, with about INR 70-odd crore of debottlenecking capex.
Polycarbonate commissioning targeted for H2 FY28-29 and BPA a couple of months later; propylene from the PDH project is expected to support phenol volumes.

Capex: about INR 1,200 crore spent to date, another INR 1,000-1,600 crore in FY27 (figures varied in the call), and about INR 3,000 crore in FY28. Peak debt estimated at INR 8,000-8,500 crore including working capital, with D/E below 1.
capex_capacity: Ammonia-to-amines integration chain (nitric acid plant, nitration and reduction) completed and stabilised; the company says it now runs 8 products simultaneously.

Phenol capacity is about 3.5 lakh tonnes, and management says it is debottlenecking toward 4 lakh tonnes through advanced process controls. Run rate reached about 1 lakh tonnes per quarter in parts of Q1, but was not sustained through the full quarter.
MIBC pre-commissioning runs reportedly exceeded design capacity; management said it can ramp above 100% once demand comes in.
Debt for the INR 11,500 crore propylene-polycarbonate project is closed, funded 60:40 debt to equity, with the 25% equity already contributed.
demand_pricing: Management said phenol demand in India is roughly balanced with no new global capacity, and some supply is short. Imports were duty-free for most of Q1 until the government reimposed the duty.
Raw material costs were high in April, but procurement secured feedstock for continuous operations. Management said feedstock costs are competitive domestically and globally.
Freight and insurance costs rose. The company responded with CIF to FOB shifts, larger parcels, and a product reformulation for a Middle East customer that changed its hazard class.
Consolidated export mix is about 20%. AI is roughly 50-50 domestic to export; Phenolics is almost entirely domestic.

qa_highlights.question: Did phenol run rate reach 1 lakh tonnes per quarter, and how is propylene covered?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 1 lakh tonnes was a run rate reached in significant periods, not the full quarter, because of raw material sourcing and a short maintenance shutdown. Debottlenecking is aimed at the 4 lakh tonne mark in the short to medium term.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Phenolics spread in Q1 and outlook for Q2-Q3?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to disclose spreads and said Deepak buys feedstock below international index levels.

qa_highlights.question: Why does the phenol capacity now exceed earlier maturity assumptions?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the main change was confidence. Advanced process controls, costing about INR 80-100 crore cumulatively, enabled higher throughput, with INR 70-odd crore more planned for debottlenecking.

qa_highlights.question: Is the phenol supply-demand balance sound?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said there is no new capacity, China is largely self-sufficient, demand is balanced and India is short of supply.

qa_highlights.question: What is the peak debt and capex plan for the INR 11,500 crore project?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR 1,200 crore has been spent. Peak borrowing is about INR 6,800 crore plus working capital, for total peak debt of INR 8,000-8,500 crore. Management said D/E will stay below 1x.

qa_highlights.question: Could you quantify incremental revenue and EBITDA margin from the new products?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to quantify, but said the margin profile of new products is in line with or above the AI average.

risks_watch: Phenol throughput depends on propylene and feedstock availability; April showed how a shutdown and raw material shortage can cut volumes.
Ramp-up timing for the Q2 AI projects and the MIBC run rate; management said the alkylation and multipurpose plants slipped because of manpower and gas shortages.
Polycarbonate and BPA commissioning (H2 FY28-29) and the debt drawdown schedule.
Freight and insurance costs and the reimposed phenol import duty could change domestic realisations.
Management declined to give Phenolics spreads, AI product-level margins, and the MIBK/acetone ratio, so these remain unverified.
summary.management_tone: Confident on the quarter and on the phenol and integration outlook, but guarded on spreads, margins and specific product economics, which management repeatedly declined to quantify. Timelines for the polycarbonate project and the AI ramp-up were described as on track but were given loosely.
key_quotes: We're no longer a nitration company that buys nitric acid. We're now a nitrogen company that nitrates.
I think the only thing that has changed is confidence.
So there is a short supply today, if I can tell you.
So, when I said 1 lakh tonnes, what I meant was on a run rate basis.
We are approved with what one would call sunrise sectors.
